text: The Burlington Sock Puppets are a summer collegiate baseball team in the Appalachian League, based in Burlington, North Carolina, and playing their home games at Burlington Athletic Stadium, commonly known as "Sockville." Professional baseball was first played in Burlington from 1958 to 1964 by the Burlington Indians, who competed in the Carolina League (Class B until 1962, then Class A) as a Cleveland Indians farm club. Twenty-two years later, from 1986 to 2006, Cleveland affiliated the team with the Appalachian League as a Rookie-level team. During the period from 2007 to 2020, the team was known as the Burlington Royals due to their affiliation with the Kansas City Royals. As part of a Minor League Baseball contraction starting in 2021, the Appalachian League was restructured into a collegiate summer baseball league for rising college freshmen and sophomores, and the Burlington Royals were renamed the Burlington Sock Puppets. The nickname reflects Burlington's historical connection to the textile industry.
